verses.1: At that time, Jesus went among the fields on Sabbaths. His disciples gathered there, picked up pebbles, and began to play with them.
verses.2: But when the Pharisees saw this, they said to him, “Look, your disciples are not doing what is proper on the Sabbath.”
verses.3: And he said to them, “Do you not know what David did when he was captured, and those who were with him?”
verses.4: How did he get into the house of God? And how did he eat the food that was prepared for him? He wasn’t allowed to eat it himself, nor were those who were with him. Only the priests were allowed to eat it.
verses.5: Don’t you know from this law that on the Sabbath days, the priests should worship in the temple, and also provide food for those who attend the services?
verses.6: I say to you that the temple is even more important.
verses.7: And if you know what it is… I want peace, not sacrifice. You certainly won’t condemn those who are unjust.
verses.8: For indeed, the Son of Man is the Lord of the Sabbath.
verses.9: And after going there, he came to their gathering.
verses.10: And they saw a man with dry hands. They asked him, “Is it permissible to heal on Sabbaths?” In order to accuse him of doing so.
verses.11: And he said to them, “Who among you would be able to raise a sheep? And if this were given to them on Saturdays, would they still be able to keep it alive?”
verses.12: So, how much does a person differ from a lamb? Therefore, it’s appropriate to do this properly on Saturdays.
verses.13: Then he said to the man, “Clench your hand.” And he clenched his hand, and he became as healthy as the other person.
verses.14: And when the Pharisees came to the council, they tried to find a way to get rid of him.
verses.15: But Jesus left that place. Many people followed him, and he healed them all.
verses.16: And he ordered that they should not reveal his identity.
verses.17: So that what was owed by Esaias, the prophet, can be paid.
verses.18: I see my son whom I have rescued from harm. He is my beloved; my soul has become fond of him. I will place my spirit upon him, and he will declare judgment over all nations.
verses.19: No one will hear his voice in the streets, nor will anyone respond to him with cries or sounds.
verses.20: It remains broken and unbroken; it doesn’t stop shining, until it is brought out into the arena for judgment.
verses.21: And they hope for that name to bring them hope.
verses.22: Then, he was afflicted with blindness and deafness. But God healed him, so that he could speak and see again.
verses.23: And all the people were astonished, and they said, “Is this really David’s son?”
verses.24: But when the Pharisees heard this, they said, “Does he not drive out demons only in Beelzebub, the chief of demons?”
verses.25: And knowing their emotions, he said to them: “All kingdoms that are divided will become barren; and all cities or homes that are divided will not stand firm.”
verses.26: And even if Satan can get rid of Satan himself, how can his kingdom then be established?
verses.27: And even if I cast out demons in Bethlehem, where do your sons cast them out? For that reason, they will become your enemies.
verses.28: But if I release the demons from the spirit of God, then the kingdom of God will come upon you.
verses.29: How can anyone enter the house of the strong man and steal his goods, if they don’t first attack the strong man first? And then they will indeed steal his house.
verses.30: He who isn’t with me is also without me, and he who doesn’t join me will be lost along with me.
verses.31: Therefore, I say to you that all sins and blasphemy will be forgiven to people. But the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.
verses.32: And whoever speaks words according to the Son of Man will be forgiven. But whoever speaks words according to the Spirit of the Holy One will not be forgiven, neither in this life nor in the future.
verses.33: Either you made the tree good, and its fruit also good; or you made the tree bad, and its fruit also bad. For it is from the fruit that the tree becomes good or bad.
verses.34: How can those who are evil be able to speak well? For it is from the excess of the heart that the mouth speaks evil.
verses.35: The good person brings out goodness from the “treasure of goodness”; the evil person, from the “treasure of evil”.
verses.36: I tell you that every excuse that people will make for being slow is a bad excuse. On the day of judgment, they will be held accountable for their actions.
verses.37: For it is through your words that you will be judged right or wrong.
verses.38: Then some of the officials and Pharisees said to him, “Teacher, we want to see some sign from you.”
verses.39: But the one who answered said to them, “You are seeking a bad and deceitful sign. She will not be given that sign unless it is the sign of Jehovah, the prophet.”
verses.40: For as Iona was in the tomb for three days and three nights, so too will the son of man be in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights.
verses.41: Men of Niveuitai will stand trial along with this family. They will be judged based on their actions. It’s clear that they were deceived by Ioannes. And indeed, Ioannes was more deceptive than anyone else.
verses.42: The Queen of the North will rise up in judgment along with this lineage. She will condemn her own people. For she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon’s wisdom. And indeed, Solomon was far greater than her.
verses.43: When the impure breath leaves a person’s body, it seeks refuge in dry places, but it cannot find any such place.
verses.44: Then he said, “I will return to my home from where I came.” When he arrived, he found his house in a state of cleanliness and ordinariness.
verses.45: Then, it also absorbs seven other more evil spirits along with itself. Once it has done this, it resides there. In this way, the rest of the human being’s nature is taken away by those seven evil spirits. Similarly, this evil spirit will also take away the rest of the person’s nature.
verses.46: And as he continued to speak to the crowd, his mother and brothers rushed outside, asking him to stop speaking.
verses.47: Someone said to him, “Look, your mother and brothers are standing outside, asking you to speak.”
verses.48: And the one who answered said to him, “Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?”
verses.49: And he stretched out his hand towards his students and said, “Look, my mother and my brothers!”
verses.50: For whoever can fulfill my father’s will in heaven, he will be my brother, sister, and mother.
